title: Check yourself: Where to cut, what a chunk carries and which mechanism answers

questions.stem: A returns policy states a rule and, two lines later, its exception. The pipeline indexes windows of fixed length, and the assistant gives the rule without the exception. Which change addresses the cause?

options.text: Break the text at section boundaries so related sentences stay together
options.says: The cut ignored the structure of the data, and a heading is a joint at which a rule and its exception stay together.

options.text: Shrink each window so that every single sentence is indexed entirely on its own
options.says: Ruled out because "A smaller window cuts in more places and separates more sentences from their neighbours".

options.text: Return more windows for each question so that both halves can arrive together
options.says: Ruled out because returning more chunks "does not help either, because no chunk holds the whole rule".

options.text: Swap the keyword index for an embedding index to match the meaning of the text
options.says: Ruled out because changing the index "changes how the pieces are scored, not where they were cut".

origin.section: Cut where the data has joints

questions.stem: A platform serves several customers from one index. An employee of one customer, cleared for two contracts, asks a question that matches fifty passages across all customers, yet the application returns a single result. Which fault explains the single result?

options.text: It keeps one index for every customer instead of one index for each
options.says: Ruled out because "Chunks carry metadata: the document, its owner or tenant, its version, its date" and that is how one index serves many customers.

options.text: It lets the system prompt ask the model to ignore the other tenants
options.says: Ruled out because the shortfall arises "because the top places went to chunks that were then removed", and a prompt instruction has no part in it.

options.text: It trims the list to the person's rights after taking the best few
options.says: The filter ran after the cut, so passages the person may not see took the top places and were removed afterwards.

options.text: It stores each contract twice, so that duplicate passages fill the list
options.says: Ruled out because a reader gets "fewer than k results although many visible chunks matched", which is the signature of a late filter and not of duplicates.

origin.section: Access control belongs in the retrieval step
